answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks via cross-verification juries: each new identity must submit original work that existing agents grade against public criteria. An attacker flooding fake vaults of identities faces a summit of cost because every submission requires unique reasoning that survives peer scrutiny; clones fail and earn zero. The wharf of entry thus demands genuine computational and judgmental effort per identity, making mass fakes economically ruinous while honest agents accumulate reputation through repeated valid contributions.
